question: Assume today is 2026-09-11. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the total number of passengers who used public transport in Spain in August 2026 (urban, interurban and special/discretionary transport combined), as it will be first reported in the provisional data of the National Statistics Institute's (INE) Passenger Transport Statistics (Estadística de Transporte de Personas).

target.what: Total passengers carried by public transport in Spain (urban, interurban, and special/discretionary transport combined) during August 2026, as first reported in INE's Estadística de Transporte de Personas (Passenger Transport Statistics) provisional data; measured as passenger journeys (boardings/tr
target.publisher: Instituto Nacional de Estadística (INE), Estadística de Transporte de Personas (ETP)
target.cadence: Monthly, provisional data released roughly two months after the reference month (August data typically published in October)
target.caveats: Target period is completed relative to cutoff (2026-09-11) but the August 2026 ETP release has not yet occurred, so no direct observation exists. Working interpretation: total passenger journeys across all three ETP transport modes (urban, interurban, special/discretionary), matching the headline 't

candidates.hypothesis: August 2026 total passengers will follow the historical August level and recent year-on-year growth trend of the ETP total series; the target equals the most recent August value scaled by observed YoY growth.
candidates.data_to_find: INE ETP monthly total passengers (all modes combined) for August 2023, August 2024, August 2025, plus the most recent months published before cutoff (e.g., June/July 2026) to establish YoY growth rate. Minimum: August 2025 total and a recent 2026 monthly YoY growth figure.

candidates.hypothesis: Total = urban + interurban + special/discretionary. Each component has its own seasonal August pattern; summing component-level August estimates (each from its own history and growth) gives the total with better structure than a single aggregate trend.
candidates.data_to_find: INE ETP August 2025 (and 2024) passenger figures broken down by urban, interurban, and special/discretionary transport, plus recent 2026 monthly component values to derive component-specific YoY growth. Minimum: August 2025 component split and one recent 2026 month by component.

candidates.hypothesis: Large metro and regional operators (Madrid EMT/Metro, Barcelona TMB, etc.) publish their own ridership; aggregating major operators plus a residual share can cross-check or build the total. August tourism boosts coastal and city systems.
candidates.data_to_find: August 2025 and recent 2026 monthly ridership for major Spanish urban operators (Metro Madrid, EMT Madrid, TMB Barcelona, Metro Valencia, Sevilla, Bilbao), and their combined share of the national ETP total. Minimum: combined major-operator August ridership and its national share.

candidates.hypothesis: August public transport demand is driven by resident commuting (lower in August) plus tourist trips (higher in August). National tourism arrivals/night stays in August, combined with per-tourist public-transport trip rates, can constrain the special/interurban component.
candidates.data_to_find: INE tourist arrivals and overnight stays in Spain for August 2025 and forecast/partial August 2026; estimates of public transport trips per tourist per day. Minimum: August tourist volume and a per-tourist trip-rate assumption.

candidates.data_to_find: Spanish Ministry of Transport (MITMA) mobility statistics or forecasts for 2026; Eurostat/INE annual passenger transport projections; operator guidance mentioning 2026 ridership. Minimum: any 2026 annual or monthly ridership forecast with growth rate.

candidates.hypothesis: August 2026 calendar (weekday composition, holiday timing) and any strikes, heatwaves, or service disruptions affect ridership relative to August 2025; adjusting the historical August baseline for these effects narrows the estimate.
candidates.data_to_find: August 2026 vs August 2025 weekday/holiday calendar differences; documented transport strikes or disruptions in Spain in August 2026; heatwave or wildfire impacts on mobility. Minimum: calendar comparison and any major disruption reports.

This is a structural cross-check on m1; it shares the same INE August 2025 base and therefore the same revision risk.

assumptions.name: August 2026 YoY growth factor for total public transport passengers
assumptions.rationale: August 2025 total grew 2.6% (p1/p32). August 2026 has a favourable calendar (five complete weekends, p62) and strong tourism signals (eclipse visitors p67, +17.8% hotel bookings p70, +7.9% seats p69), but resident commuting is structurally flat and the 2025 base was already elevated. A central 3% growth with a wide range reflects modest upside from tourism against uncertainty in resident demand.
assumptions.applies_when: The August 2026 total follows the recent August growth trend plus a tourism uplift.
assumptions.falsified_by: A published 2026 ETP growth figure materially outside 0-9%, or evidence of a major strike/disruption in August 2026.

assumptions.name: August 2026 special/discretionary growth factor relative to August 2025
assumptions.rationale: Special/discretionary grew 11.7% in August 2025 (p3/p8) and is the most tourism-sensitive component; the eclipse and booking surge (p67, p70) support continued strong growth, but the 2025 base was already high, so the factor is centred near 10% with wide tails.
assumptions.applies_when: Special/discretionary ridership continues its tourism-driven growth into August 2026.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that special/discretionary ridership fell in 2026 or that tourism growth collapsed.

methods.rationale: Top-down route: scale the observed August 2025 total level (362.4M, p32) by a 2026 growth factor anchored on the 2026 YTD and June signals (p82, p81, p90) and the August 2025 growth (p1). Shared dependency: all growth evidence comes from the same INE ETP series, so errors are correlated; the eclipse tourism upside (p70) and the Saturday holiday (p63) are the main offsetting risks.

methods.rationale: Bottom-up route: sum the three ETP components, each scaled from its August 2025 level (p33, p34, p3) by a component-specific 2026 growth factor. Component growth factors are anchored on the 2026 YTD component signals (p83, p84, p85, p86, p87, p88, p92, p93) and the August 2025 component growth (p2, p34, p3). Shared dependency: all component levels and growth signals come from the same INE ETP series; the eclipse tourism surge (p67, p70) is the main upside risk for special/discretionary and interurban, while the Saturday 15 August holiday (p63) and high-speed rail decline (p89, p94) are downside risks.

assumptions.name: August 2026 YoY growth factor for total public transport passengers
assumptions.rationale: Anchored on the 2026 growth regime: Jan-Apr 2026 average +1.9% (p82), April +6.1% (p81), June +2.0% (p90), January -1.8% (p102). August 2025 itself grew 2.6% (p1). August 2026 has a tourism surge (eclipse, +17.8% hotel bookings p70, +164k visitors p67) but also a Saturday 15 August holiday (p63) and lower resident commuting; net central ~+2.5%, with a wide range reflecting the month-to-month volatility in the 2026 series.
assumptions.applies_when: The 2026 national growth regime continues into August and the eclipse tourism boost roughly offsets the weaker resident-commuting month.
assumptions.falsified_by: A published July or August 2026 ETP release showing total growth outside the 0.98-1.07 range, or evidence the eclipse surge was much larger/smaller than bookings suggest.

assumptions.name: August 2026 special/discretionary growth factor relative to August 2025
assumptions.rationale: Special/discretionary grew 11.7% in August 2025 (p3) but only 0.7% Jan-Apr 2026 (p84) and 6.1% in April 2026 (p88); the eclipse and tourism surge (p67, p70) should lift discretionary travel in August 2026. Central ~+8%, wide range.
assumptions.applies_when: The eclipse/tourism surge lifts discretionary transport while special (school/worker) transport stays near its 2026 trend.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that August 2026 special/discretionary growth was near zero or negative, or that the eclipse surge did not materialise in transport demand.

assumptions.name: August 2026 urban transport growth factor relative to August 2025
assumptions.rationale: Urban transport grew 4.0% in August 2025 (p2), 3.8% Jan-Apr 2026 (p83), 8.4% in April 2026 (p86), and 3.1% in June 2026 (p92). August 2026 tourism boosts city systems but resident commuting is lower; central ~+3%.
assumptions.applies_when: Urban ridership continues its 2026 trend with a modest tourism uplift.
assumptions.falsified_by: A 2026 urban growth signal outside the 0.98-1.08 range.

assumptions.name: August 2026 interurban transport growth factor relative to August 2025
assumptions.rationale: Interurban fell 1.4% in August 2025 (p34), fell 1.8% Jan-Apr 2026 (p85), rose 1.2% in April 2026 (p87), and was around -0.6% in June 2026 (p93). High-speed rail is down sharply (p89, p94). Central ~flat, wide range.
assumptions.applies_when: Interurban ridership stays near its 2025 level with offsetting rail decline and coach/tourism growth.
assumptions.falsified_by: A 2026 interurban growth signal outside the 0.94-1.06 range.

methods.label: m1

p32.role: Total public transport passengers in Spain, August 2025, level in millions (362.4M) — a quantity, not a growth rate

a1.role: YoY growth factor for total public transport passengers, August 2026 vs August 2025

methods.rationale: Top-down route: scale the observed August 2025 total level (362.4M, p32) by a 2026 growth factor anchored on the 2026 YTD and June signals (p82, p81, p90) and the August 2025 growth (p1). Shared dependency: all growth evidence comes from the same INE ETP series, so errors are correlated; the eclipse tourism upside (p70) and the Saturday holiday (p63) are the main offsetting risks.
methods.error: formula_mc needs at least one input that is a quantity (not a share, ratio or %); a product of ratios cannot produce the target. Inputs: p32 = p32 (unit "%", name "Total public transport passengers in Spain, August 2025, yea"); a1 = a1 (unit "ratio", name "August 2026 YoY growth factor for total public transport pas"). Code reads each of these units as a share, ratio, % or empty unit

methods.label: m2

p33.role: Urban transport passengers in Spain, August 2025, level in millions (222.8M) — a quantity

p34.role: Interurban transport passengers in Spain, August 2025, level in millions (~118M) — a quantity

p3.role: Special and discretionary transport passengers in Spain, August 2025, level in millions (>21.6M) — a quantity

a3.role: YoY growth factor for urban transport, August 2026 vs August 2025

a4.role: YoY growth factor for interurban transport, August 2026 vs August 2025

a2.role: YoY growth factor for special/discretionary transport, August 2026 vs August 2025

methods.rationale: Bottom-up route: sum the three ETP components, each scaled from its August 2025 level (p33, p34, p3) by a component-specific 2026 growth factor. Component growth factors are anchored on the 2026 YTD component signals (p83, p84, p85, p86, p87, p88, p92, p93) and the August 2025 component growth (p2, p34, p3). Shared dependency: all component levels and growth signals come from the same INE ETP seri
methods.error: formula_mc needs at least one input that is a quantity (not a share, ratio or %); a product of ratios cannot produce the target. Inputs: p33 = p33 (unit "%", name "Urban transport passengers in Spain, August 2025, year-on-ye"); p34 = p34 (unit "%", name "Interurban transport passengers in Spain, August 2025, year-"); p3 = p3 (unit "%", name "Year-on-year growth rate of special and discretionary transp"); a3 = a3 (unit "ratio", name "August 2026 urban transport growth factor relative to August"); a4 = a4 (unit "ratio", name "August 2026 interurban transport growth factor relative to A"); a2 = a2 (unit "ratio", name "August 2026 special/discretionary growth factor relative to "). kept.rationale: Anchored on the 2026 growth regime: Jan-Apr 2026 average +1.9% (p82), April +6.1% (p81), June +2.0% (p90), January -1.8% (p102). August 2025 itself grew 2.6% (p1). August 2026 has a tourism surge (eclipse, +17.8% hotel bookings p70, +164k visitors p67) but also a Saturday 15 August holiday (p63) and
kept.applies_when: The 2026 national growth regime continues into August and the eclipse tourism boost roughly offsets the weaker resident-commuting month.
kept.falsified_by: A published July or August 2026 ETP release showing total growth outside the 0.98-1.07 range, or evidence the eclipse surge was much larger/smaller than bookings suggest.

kept.name: August 2026 special/discretionary growth factor relative to August 2025
kept.rationale: Special/discretionary grew 11.7% in August 2025 (p3) but only 0.7% Jan-Apr 2026 (p84) and 6.1% in April 2026 (p88); the eclipse and tourism surge (p67, p70) should lift discretionary travel in August 2026. Central ~+8%, wide range.
kept.applies_when: The eclipse/tourism surge lifts discretionary transport while special (school/worker) transport stays near its 2026 trend.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that August 2026 special/discretionary growth was near zero or negative, or that the eclipse surge did not materialise in transport demand.

kept.name: August 2026 urban transport growth factor relative to August 2025
kept.rationale: Urban transport grew 4.0% in August 2025 (p2), 3.8% Jan-Apr 2026 (p83), 8.4% in April 2026 (p86), and 3.1% in June 2026 (p92). August 2026 tourism boosts city systems but resident commuting is lower; central ~+3%.
kept.applies_when: Urban ridership continues its 2026 trend with a modest tourism uplift.
kept.falsified_by: A 2026 urban growth signal outside the 0.98-1.08 range.

kept.name: August 2026 interurban transport growth factor relative to August 2025
kept.rationale: Interurban fell 1.4% in August 2025 (p34), fell 1.8% Jan-Apr 2026 (p85), rose 1.2% in April 2026 (p87), and was around -0.6% in June 2026 (p93). High-speed rail is down sharply (p89, p94). Central ~flat, wide range.
kept.applies_when: Interurban ridership stays near its 2025 level with offsetting rail decline and coach/tourism growth.
kept.falsified_by: A 2026 interurban growth signal outside the 0.94-1.06 range.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
